Pain points: double data entry, trust banking setup, manual reconciliation totals, and co-host split payouts that don't match statement math.
Co-hosts reconcile Airbnb split payouts in spreadsheets outside the PMS.

Counter-evidence: Hospitable, Hostaway and OwnerRez already provide owner statements; Hospitable added co-host statements and payouts; one 30-unit manager says OwnerRez reports cover most needs; templates work for a handful of owners.
Price drift between PriceLabs/PMS and Airbnb/Vrbo is real and recurring: Vrbo feed lag, Airbnb promotions stopping sync, batch rejections over a 10% jump, PMS broadcast delays.
Many cases trace to one-off configuration errors fixable by reconnecting, and PMSs show price sources per day.
Hosts handle drift by writing to PMS helpdesks, escalating to Airbnb support, reconfiguring connections or turning the pricing tool off.
Vrbo sync edge cases on Guesty require manual cleanup per review aggregation.
Lock-code failures happen (code mismatch locking a guest out, no retry button, confusing backup codes, last-minute timing gaps).
Airbnb and Hospitable already alert on offline locks or patch the issues themselves; frequency of failures is unknown.
Cost sensitivity is visible: managers want to avoid extra subscriptions, and transaction/booking fees on Hostaway draw criticism.
An owner-portal/statement add-on already exists at $49/month (OwnerCenter), the same price as the hypothesis.
Support quality is a recurring complaint for Guesty.
In small operations the manager/co-host runs and pays for the stack themselves (e.g., a licensed manager with 30 condos handling payouts).
The co-host pool is growing on Airbnb's network (10,000 at launch, 20,000 more interested).

new_unknowns.question: What share of 5-50 listing co-hosts already use Hospitable/OwnerRez owner statements and still reconcile Airbnb split payouts by hand?
How often does PriceLabs-to-channel price drift cause a mispriced booking per listing per year, and what does it cost?

current_solutions.statement: Incumbent PMSs (Hospitable, Hostaway, OwnerRez) already ship owner statements and owner portals; Hospitable added co-host statements and native owner payouts.
Where the PMS falls short, managers bolt on accounting tools (QuickBooks, Clearing, VRPlatform, OwnerCenter) or reconcile in spreadsheets.
Airbnb itself splits co-host payouts per booking, so the residual work is reconciling other channels and the true-up, not the whole statement.
Price/calendar drift is handled by support tickets, reconfiguring connections or turning the pricing tool off; no dedicated watchdog appeared in the evidence.
